memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: Independent in activities of daily living, continues to drive her auto-rickshaw, reports occasional brief vertigo episodes lasting seconds.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 4 out of 5 (three-word recall intact, clock drawing normal).
falls: No falls in the last 12 months; gait steady; timed up-and-go 10 seconds.
medicines: 4 regular – betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS, levetiracetam 500 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD.
mood: Reports good mood, denies depression or anxiety.
carers: Ramesh, husband.
goals: "I want to keep driving safely and manage my vertigo."

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum sodium: 138 mmol/L (reference 135-145).
Serum creatinine: 0.9 mg/L (reference 0.6-1.1).
Both within normal limits.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
Betahistine 16 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.
Meclizine 25 mg tablet – take one tablet as needed for vertigo, max three times daily.
Levetiracetam 500 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.
Lamotrigine 50 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: EEG: Awake and asleep recording shows no epileptiform discharges; background activity normal for age. No seizure activity captured.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past three weeks I have had two brief spinning sensations when turning my head quickly while driving. Each lasted less than a minute and resolved on its own. No loss of consciousness or headache.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: Still drives auto-rickshaw; notes vertigo episodes reduced to once per week, mild.
cognition: Mini-Cog not repeated (annual screen due next visit).
falls: No falls in past 12 months; gait smooth; timed up-and-go 9 seconds.
medicines: 4 regular – betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS, levetiracetam 500 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD.
mood: Reports occasional frustration with vertigo but overall content.
carers: Ramesh, husband.
goals: "I aim to reduce vertigo to rare episodes and continue working."

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum sodium: 137 mmol/L (reference 135-145).
Serum creatinine: 0.9 mg/L (reference 0.6-1.1).
Stable from previous.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
Levetiracetam dose increased to 750 mg tablet twice daily due to occasional breakthrough sensation reported.
All other medications unchanged: betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS, lamotrigine 50 mg BD.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow-up visit booked for 15 October 2025 at 10:00 am with Dr Nandini Kulkarni (D06). Patient confirmed via clinic app.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: Driving continues; vertigo episodes now infrequent, only occasional mild light‑headedness.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 3/5 (two-word recall delayed, clock drawing normal) – positive screen (<=2? actually 3 >2, so negative). Falls: No falls in past 12 months; gait steady; timed up-and-go 10 seconds.
medicines: 5 regular – betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS, levetiracetam 750 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD, vitamin D3 1000 IU daily (added for bone health).
Polypharmacy noted (5 medicines); request review against Beers criteria.
mood: Reports good sleep and mood.
carers: Ramesh, husband.
goals: "I want to stay independent and avoid any falls."

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Audiometry: Pure‑tone averages 25 dB HL in left ear, 28 dB HL in right ear (mild high‑frequency loss). No conductive component. Results consistent with age‑related changes; no pathology contributing to vertigo.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: Continues auto‑rickshaw work; reports no vertigo spells in past two months.
cognition: Mini-Cog repeated (annual) – score 4/5 (three-word recall intact, clock drawing normal).
falls: No falls in last 12 months; gait smooth; timed up-and-go 9 seconds.
medicines: 4 regular – betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS, levetiracetam 750 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD (vitamin D3 stopped after normal levels).
mood: Stable, denies depression.
carers: Ramesh, husband.
goals: "My goal is to remain seizure‑free and keep working without interruption."
